items.text:
I completed a **4,600-word company analysis using 51 cited sources**, covering ownership, finances, products, customers, leadership, patents, hiring, competitors and risks.

[Read the full NOVELIC report](/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/novelic-company-analysis.md) · [Source index and original documents](/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/source-index.md)

**My assessment: NOVELIC is a credible radar and embedded engineering company, but its latest financial performance is weak. Its prospects depend heavily on converting automotive design wins into profitable production.**

The most important findings, as of **7 September 2026**:

- **Ownership is clear.** Sona Comstar acquired 54% in September 2023 for an adjusted **€40.097 million**; the founders retained approximately 46%. The completed transaction is documented in the [stock-exchange disclosure](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SONACOMS_04092023225204_Intimation.pdf). The original announcement provides historical valuation context, rather than a current valuation: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/acquisition-2023.pdf" purpose="source"}.

- **Its technical credentials have substance.** Products cover in-cabin monitoring, exterior automotive radar, building occupancy and industrial/robotic sensing. Relationships are independently confirmed by [Infineon](https://www.infineon.com/partners/design-partner/novelic) and [Lattice](https://www.latticesemi.com/Support/Partners/NOVELIC). These validate the engineering ecosystem, while leaving sales volumes and profitability undisclosed.

- **Named commercial references exist.** NOVELIC publishes customer projects involving [VBG Coupling](https://www.novelic.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/NIC_MCS_VBG_Spread_20231012_v2.pdf) and [Firefly](https://www.novelic.com/blog/case-study-powering-seamless-smart-lighting-control-with-human-presence-detection-for-firefly/). Its major automotive Tier 1 nomination remains unnamed, with no public unit pricing or committed volumes.

The clearest concern is financial. The NOVELIC group’s signed consolidation schedules show:

| RSD millions | Year ended March 2025 | Year ended March 2026 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 1,097.7 | 903.7 |
| Net profit / loss | 7.1 | **−218.3** |
| Operating cash flow | −145.6 | **−160.9** |
| Cash plus short-term financial assets | 334.2 | **80.9** |

Revenue fell **17.7%**, and the latest net loss equalled **24.2% of revenue**. I checked the scanned tables in :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/novelic-fy2025.pdf" purpose="source"} and :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/novelic-fy2026.pdf" purpose="source"}. These are signed schedules; the parent’s audited annual-report package separately corroborates a substantial subsidiary loss: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/parent-fy2026-consolidated.pdf" purpose="source"}.

**Production progress is encouraging, but the economics remain unproven publicly.** The India subsidiary’s accounts confirm the new entity: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/novelic-india-fy2026.pdf" purpose="source"}. In April 2026, Sona said its first India customer launch targeted production at the **end of calendar 2026**, with SMT equipment already installed: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/parent-q4fy2026-call.pdf" purpose="source"}. Public sources do not establish achieved automotive shipment volumes or production margins.

Sona’s broader robotics strategy gives NOVELIC additional opportunities, including the parent’s Neura Robotics collaboration: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/parent-fy2026-board.pdf" purpose="source"}. In July, Sona disclosed robotics, AMR engineering and commercial-vehicle radar wins. Its **INR 8 billion Robotics and Physical AI order book belongs to the parent’s broader business category**; it cannot be attributed entirely to NOVELIC: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/graovic/pulsarpoint/ppoint/output/research/novelic-2026-09-07/sources/parent-q1fy2027-call.pdf" purpose="source"}.

For a partnership or procurement decision, NOVELIC merits technical evaluation. For an investment or substantial financial commitment, the decisive missing information is **current cash availability, customer concentration, actual production status, product margins and committed shareholder support**. The full report documents these gaps and flags conflicting website specifications, certification claims and financial reporting periods.
